cards.text: Job's friend Zophar the Naamathite has just finished his speech (Job 11:1), and now Job answers: "Truly then you are the people with whom wisdom itself will die!" Ohhh, friend, when a man opens with "truly," you KNOW the next part is gonna sting.

cards.question: Right after that line about wisdom dying with his friends, Job says, "But I also have a mind; I am not inferior to you." True or false: Job really thinks his friends are the wisest people alive.

cards.text: Then Job talks about where he stands with these friends. He says he called on God, and God answered him.

cards.question: Job called on God, and God answered. But Job says that to his friends, he has become a ___.

cards.text: Job says the one at ease scorns misfortune as the fate of those whose feet are slipping. Real easy to yell at the players from the couch, friend.

cards.question: Job says the righteous man is a laughingstock. Meanwhile, the tents of ___ are safe, and those who provoke God are secure.

cards.text: Then Job sends his friends to some new teachers: the animals, the birds of the air, the earth and the fish of the sea. Friend, he just told these guys to go take notes from a FISH.

cards.question: Job says the animals, the birds, the earth and the fish all know something. What do they all know?

answers.text: The hand of the LORD has done this
The LORD has rested from His work
The LORD is far from His creatures

cards.text: Job says the life of every living thing is in God's hand, along with the breath of all mankind. Every sparrow, every goldfish, every guy honking in traffic, ALL in one hand.

cards.question: Job compares the ear hearing words to the tongue tasting its food. What is he saying a person should do with the words they hear?

answers.text: Repeat them to everyone they meet
Forget them as soon as they hear them

cards.text: Job says wisdom is found with the elderly, and understanding comes with long life. Makes sense. It took me YEARS in a junk drawer just to learn how to sit still.

cards.question: Job just said understanding comes with long life. Then he goes higher: wisdom and strength belong to ___.

cards.text: When God tears something down, friend, nobody's putting it back together. What He tears down can't be rebuilt, and the man He imprisons can't be released.

cards.question: Job says even the waters answer to God. When He holds them back, they dry up. True or false: when He releases them, they overwhelm the land.
Job says true wisdom and power belong to God. True or false: Job says only the deceived belong to God.

cards.text: Then Job goes down a list of the most powerful people around: counselors, judges, kings, priests, elders, nobles and the mighty. Friend, this is the VIP section. Velvet rope and everything.

cards.question: Counselors, judges, kings, priests, elders, nobles and the mighty. What does Job say God can do to every one of these powerful people?

answers.text: Bring every one of them low
Give every one of them more power
Turn every one of them against Job

cards.text: Job says God reveals the deep things of darkness and brings deep shadows into light, and He makes nations great and destroys them. Friend, He found me at the back of a JUNK DRAWER, so deep shadows? Easy work.

cards.question: Job says God can take away the reason of the earth's leaders and make them wander in a trackless wasteland, groping in the darkness without light. How does Job say they move?

cards.text: Job's still talking to his friends. His eyes have seen all this, his ears have heard it, and whatever they know, he knows too. Translation: I read the same manual, fellas.

cards.question: Job's done comparing notes with his friends. Who does he really want to argue his case before?

cards.text: Then Job turns back to his friends, and he does NOT hold back. He says they smear with lies.

cards.question: Job says his friends smear with lies. He calls all of them worthless ___.
Job says there's one thing his friends could do that would actually be their wisdom: remain ___.

cards.text: Friend, that is the oldest way there is to say PLEASE stop talking. Then Job asks if they'll speak wickedly on God's behalf, or show Him partiality.

cards.question: Job asks his friends if they could deceive God the way they'd deceive a man. True or false: Job says God would rebuke them for secretly showing partiality.

cards.text: Then Job asks if God's majesty wouldn't terrify them, and if the dread of Him wouldn't fall on them. That's the kind of question that makes ANYBODY sit up straight.

cards.question: Job tells his friends their maxims are proverbs of ashes and their defenses are defenses of clay. What's he saying about their arguments?

answers.text: They are too deep to follow

cards.text: Job tells them, "Be silent, and I will speak. Then let come to me what may." He asks why he puts himself at risk and takes his life in his own hands.

cards.question: Job knows speaking up to God is a risk. But even if God slays him, what does Job say he'll do?
Job will hope in God even if God slays him. True or false: Job says he'll still defend his ways to God's face.

cards.text: Job says this will be his salvation, because no godless man can appear before God. Then he tells his friends to listen carefully and let his words ring in their ears.

cards.question: Job says he has prepared his case, and he knows that he will be ___.
Job asks if anyone can indict him. True or false: Job says if someone can, he'll argue even louder.

cards.text: And that's where we'll pause, friend. Trust me, this conversation is FAR from over.

findings.problem: The setup only says that Job called on God and God answered. Nothing in the earlier cards indicates that Job's friends ridicule him, so choosing "laughingstock" over "stranger" or "burden" requires guessing an unseen word rather than reasoning out the meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The setup says only that Job's friends smear with lies. It gives no basis for choosing "physicians" over "shepherds" or "builders," so the blank depends on guessing the wording of Job 13:4.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
